ingredients.name: Toor, chana and moong dal, mixed

steps.text: Mix the flour, semolina, salt and ajwain, crushing the ajwain between your palms.
Rub in plenty of ghee until a fistful holds together when pressed.
steps.her_cue: मुट्ठी में दबाओ तो लड्डू जैसा बंध जाए

steps.text: Add water little by little and knead a stiff dough. Cover and rest 10 minutes.
Shape small balls and press the centre lightly with your thumb.
steps.her_cue: बीच में अंगूठे से हल्का सा दबा देना

steps.text: Bake at 200 °C, turning often, until golden and starting to crack.
steps.her_cue: जब तक सुनहरी न हो जाए और फटने लगे

steps.text: Dip the hot baatis in melted ghee.
Pressure-cook the mixed dal with turmeric and salt for three whistles.
For the tadka, heat ghee and add cumin, hing and red chilli.
steps.her_cue: Jab tak jeera chatakne na lage

steps.text: Add onion and tomato and fry the masala.
steps.her_cue: जब तक तेल न छोड़ दे

steps.text: Pour the tadka into the dal and let it boil with the lid on.
Finish with hara dhaniya and a little nimbu.

tips: Be generous with ghee in the dough (khoob saara ghee); the moyan makes the baati crisp.
A tandoor is even better than the oven.
warnings: Don't open the lid while the dal boils, it will boil over (dhakkan mat kholna).
The dough must be stiff, not soft (naram nahi).
quotes: खाना हमेशा प्यार से बनाओ, स्वाद अपने आप आता है।
हाथ से ही आता है अंदाज़
Dal baati is the taste of Rajasthan.
ask_next_time: How long do the baatis bake in the oven?
How much water goes in the cooker with the dal?
Whole red chillies or chilli powder in the tadka?
How many baatis does this make?
